1	/**
     2	 * Workspace Detail View — Repo Parallelizer GUI.
     3	 *
     4	 * Renders the full detail page for a single workspace inside a project:
     5	 *   - Workspace header: ID, description, breadcrumb link back to the project.
     6	 *   - Repository status table: one row per repository, showing current branch,
     7	 *     a color-coded Git status badge, an error/loading indicator for repos
     8	 *     with no status data yet, and an Actions column containing an "Open"
     9	 *     button that opens the repository in GitHub Desktop via
    10	 *     `api.workspaces.launch.githubDesktop(projectId, wid, repoId)`.
    11	 *   - Live polling: status badges refresh in-place via a 1-second countdown
    12	 *     interval that triggers a poll every 10 seconds. A visible countdown
    13	 *     label and a "Refresh Now" button provide user control. The interval
    14	 *     is cleared via the cleanup function returned from
    15	 *     `renderWorkspaceDetail`, which the router calls before navigating
    16	 *     away.
    17	 *   - Actions: "Open in VS Code" button (shown only when workspace is
    18	 *     initialised, dynamically added after a successful Setup — calls
    19	 *     `api.workspaces.launch.vscode`), "Switch Branches" navigation button,
    20	 *     "Rename Workspace" (disabled for STABLE), "Delete Workspace" (disabled
    21	 *     for STABLE).
    22	 *
    23	 * ## Credential-error display
    24	 *
    25	 * When a repository's clone fails because no credential is configured for its
    26	 * host, the setup orchestrators emit an error message containing the sentinel
    27	 * text defined by `CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL` ("requires a credential for
    28	 * host"). The view detects this via `applySetupResultCredentialErrors()` and
    29	 * replaces the generic "No data" badge in the status table with an amber
    30	 * "Missing Credential" badge (`.status-badge-credential`) that links directly
    31	 * to `#/repositories/:id` so the user can assign a credential without leaving
    32	 * the workflow.
    33	 *
    34	 * Key helpers in this subsystem:
    35	 *   - `CREDENTIAL_MISSING_SENTINEL` — the exact string matched against error
    36	 *     messages. Defined in `gui/public/js/utils/constants.js`; imported here.
    37	 *     Must stay in sync with the orchestrator error templates.
    38	 *   - `buildMissingCredentialBadge(repoId)` — renders the amber `<a>` badge
    39	 *     (`.status-badge-credential`) and wires SPA navigation via `_router`
    40	 *     (with `href` as a fallback). **Distinct from `buildCredentialBadge()`
    41	 *     in `utils/dom.js`:** this badge is an `<a>` element that signals a
    42	 *     *clone failure* in the workspace status table and links to the
    43	 *     repository settings page; `buildCredentialBadge()` is a `<span>` that
    44	 *     shows the *assignment status* of a credential in the repository list
    45	 *     (`.credential-badge--set` / `.credential-badge--none`). The two badges
    46	 *     serve different views and must not be conflated.
    47	 *   - `applySetupResultCredentialErrors(setupResult)` — called after every
    48	 *     setup invocation (Setup button, Retry Setup, health alert) to add or
    49	 *     remove repos from the in-memory `credentialErrorRepoIds` Set and update
    50	 *     their badge cell in the DOM immediately.
    51	 *   - `applyStatusMapUpdate()` — clears the credential-error flag when a repo
    52	 *     transitions from no-data to having live status data (i.e. after a
    53	 *     successful re-clone following credential assignment).
    54	 *
    55	 * **Known limitation:** `credentialErrorRepoIds` is an in-memory Set populated
    56	 * only by explicit `setup()` calls during the current page session. If the page
    57	 * is reloaded after a prior credential-missing failure, the badge will not
    58	 * appear until the next Setup run because the error state is not persisted in
    59	 * the workspace health report or the status map. Surfacing this on page load
    60	 * would require a new API endpoint or server-side persistence — out of scope
    61	 * for the current implementation.
    62	 *
    63	 * ## Router integration
    64	 *
    65	 * The view uses the same router-injection pattern as `project-detail.js`:
    66	 * `app.js` calls `setRouter(router)` before `router.start()`. The `_router`

    69	 *
    70	 * ## Cleanup contract

    72	 * `renderWorkspaceDetail` returns a cleanup function. The router's `_render`
